children: After a brief lull ahead of the Diwali festive season, India’s primary market is poised for a strong revival, with 29 companies expected to raise nearly ₹42,000 crore through initial public offerings (IPOs) by the end of the year.

Among the major IPO lined up before December are Carlsberg India (₹6,650 crore), Avaada Electro (₹6,000 crore), and Cult.fit (₹4,000 crore). Svatantra Microfin and Encube Ethicals are also expected to raise around ₹3,000 crore each, according to market participants.

VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments said after the mega IPOs of NSE and Jio Platforms, the IPO market has cooled a bit, but now that the secondary market has bounced back strongly, there will be renewed interest in IPOs.
“Market is keenly awaiting tech IPOs of Zepto, Razorpay and PhonePay which are likely to witness good response if the pricing is right,” he said.

Despite the recent global equity market sell-off, Indian markets have remained relatively resilient, helping restore investor confidence. Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have turned net buyers, pumping ₹1.15 lakh crore into Indian equities so far this month, compared with a net outflow of ₹34,843 crore in October.

Investor sentiment in the primary market has also strengthened. FPIs have invested ₹452 crore in IPOs and other primary market issuances this month, compared with ₹9,722 crore in October, when Jio Platforms launched the country’s largest-ever IPO.

The resurgence in FPI flows into India comes even as global markets grapple with concerns over the sustainability of massive investments in artificial intelligence, which have triggered sharp corrections in several overseas equity markets.

Rajesh Singla, Founder and Fund Manager at Alpha AMC, said companies have already raised about ₹1.58 lakh crore through IPOs so far this year until October, despite secondary markets remaining subdued for much of the period.

“This demonstrates that companies are not waiting for ideal market conditions to tap investors. More importantly, investors continue to back businesses with strong fundamentals and growth prospects,” he said.

Singla noted that the IPO pipeline remains robust, with around 252 companies reportedly planning to raise nearly ₹4.5 lakh crore. Of these, 121 companies have already secured regulatory approvals and are waiting for an opportune market window to launch their offerings.

Gurmeet Singh Chawla, Managing Director at Master Portfolio Services, said that more than 120 companies are currently holding valid approvals from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), including several large and well-recognised corporate names.
“A bulk of the activity is likely to be concentrated in the first two to three weeks of December,” Chawla said.

He added that market activity typically slows during the final stretch of the year, particularly from Christmas week through the first few days of January. “Companies are likely to wait for a cleaner issuance window once activity resumes in January, but the pipeline remains strong and ready for launch,” he said.

title: IPO Street set for year-end revival; 29 firms eye ₹42,000 crore as sentiment improves
